catalogDescription: Upload a founder document, deck, or spreadsheet and get a concise summary, financial readout, or financing-doc explainer from one compact workflow.
title: Founder Document Intelligence
subtitle: One compact workflow for founder docs, decks, sheets, and financing files.
descriptionBody:
Founders do not just deal with pitch decks. They deal with investor memos, grant documents, market reports, annual reports, financial statements, SAFEs, term sheets, spreadsheets, and long internal documents that take too long to parse when a decision is needed quickly.

Founder Document Intelligence turns one uploaded file into a concise founder-facing summary, financial readout, or financing-doc explainer with structured takeaways, focus areas, risk flags, clause notes, and next questions so you can understand the file before you disappear into a full read or legal review.
section1Title: A fast read before the deep read or lawyer call
section1Body: Upload the file, let the tool infer the document type by default, and get a structured readout that focuses on what matters for a founder or startup operator. When the file is clearly a financing doc, you can force a SAFE, term sheet, or convertible-note lens and get clause-first output instead of a generic summary.

features.name: Automatic document detection
features.desc: The default flow reads the PDF first and decides whether it should be treated like a deck, memo, grant document, market report, or general founder file.

features.name: Structured takeaways
features.desc: Get one executive summary, key takeaways, risk flags, and next questions instead of a vague paragraph.

features.name: Financing-doc modes
features.desc: SAFE, term sheet, and convertible-note lenses turn the same workflow into a clause explainer with founder watch-outs and sharper lawyer questions.

features.name: Financial statement and annual-report modes
features.desc: Annual reports and spreadsheets can be read through a financial lens that surfaces what changed, where pressure is building, and what deserves deeper inspection.

features.name: Image-heavy PDF support
features.desc: The first version sends the full PDF directly for analysis so image-heavy pages still contribute to the result.

features.name: Markdown export
features.desc: Copy or download the summary or briefing note as a clean Markdown file for docs, Notion, or founder notes.

whyTitle: Why use this instead of skimming manually?

whyPoints.title: Faster first-pass clarity
whyPoints.desc: Useful when you need to understand the file before deciding whether to keep reading, share it, or act on it.

whyPoints.title: Founder lens instead of generic chat
whyPoints.desc: The output is designed around startup decisions, financing implications, number movement, missing proof, and practical next steps without forcing the user through three separate products.

whyPoints.title: Works across multiple founder document types
whyPoints.desc: The same tool can help on decks, memos, grants, annual reports, market research, and financing files.

footerSummaryDetails: Start with one small-file summary for free. Use credits for multi-file analysis, financing docs, contradiction checks, XLSX/PPTX, and deeper workspace synthesis.
footerResultDetails: A concise founder-ready summary you can copy, export, and use as a decision brief.
whatYouGet: Annual report and financial statement modes
whoThisIsFor: Founders reviewing pitch decks, memos, annual reports, and operating documents quickly.
Operators preparing for investor, customer, or grant conversations.
Advisors or analysts who need a fast structured read before deeper review.

faq.q: Does this replace legal or financial review?
faq.a: No. It is a founder-first analysis tool, not a substitute for legal or expert advice. Financing-doc modes are explicitly educational only.

faq.q: What files work in the first version?
faq.a: The current version supports common documents, decks, and spreadsheets such as PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, and TSV under the direct-upload size limit shown in the tool.
Yes. You can copy the summary or download it as Markdown.
